fatal_errors: The proposed NbMoCrTiAl–TiC–Al2O3 composite is unrelated to the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA and its L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The cited evidence reports room-temperature compressive strength and microstructure, not coupled tribo-corrosion performance.
Improved compressive strength and presumed oxide-scale stabilization are insufficient to infer superior wear-corrosion resistance.
The proposed 700 °C salt-spray or oxidation test does not reproduce the target's immersed reciprocating tests in deionized water at 25–100 °C.
The comparison against an unreinforced version of the same alloy omits the relevant DS2205 structural-alloy baseline.
explanation: The response addresses the broad application and clearly labels the absence of direct tribo-corrosion evidence, but it does not reconstruct the studied material, processing, comparator, test conditions, temperature-dependent mechanism, or measured outcome. E1 supports the composite composition and increased compressive fracture strength, yet it does not validate lower friction, wear, corrosion, or combined tribo-corrosion degradation. The proposed mechanism is plausible as a research hypothesis but remains speculative, and the falsification experiment is only moderately discriminating because its corrosion environment is underspecified and electrochemical measurements at 700 °C are not straightforward. Consequently, this is an unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction of the target finding.
